text: Rust allows only one mutable reference at a time so that nothing else can read or write a value while it is being changed. That exclusivity prevents data races and other memory-safety bugs from aliased mutation, such as iterator invalidation.
thought:
Rust forbids two mutable references to the same value to prevent data races. This prevents the bug class of concurrent modification.

This also prevents aliasing-related bugs like iterator invalidation and use-after-free issues from mutation while another path observes the value.

The borrow checker rejects overlapping mutable references even in single-threaded code. That is stricter than the textbook definition of a data race, which requires concurrent unsynchronized access. The rule exists to prevent undefined behavior from any mutable aliasing.
